title: Wickliffe's repertoire: Dixieland numbers, blues and rags
summary: The band played Tiger Rag, Panama, blues in the trumpeter's key, popular tunes and rags with piano features.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Did Wycliffe use Dixieland numbers? They were very popular then.

Oh, well, we had Tiger Reg, and you know, with Fidgety Feet, and, well, four or five other numbers that were published for the first time. But, you know, the original Dixieland. Panama became a... Panama, oh yes, Panama. We played that, yeah, Panama.
It wasn't really from Dixie sources, I think, a higher up there.
Yeah, it was, it was, it had a slightly Spanish pattern. Yeah. A slight...
And you had the blues, all the famous New Orleans type of...

Yeah, we had, we played, well, see, the man that we were going to feature in the blues, he picked these keys. He said, all right, the blues and B flat. Now, maybe that, that, we wouldn't live, Klan, most of that. Well, all right, that was his blues. All right, trumpet player, he, maybe he played his blues and concert E flat. And we'd play that, and he'd take it for his own. He'd take the circle of course, and then finally some of them, I'd play blues on the violin, and somebody would answer it. And, in other words, the trumpet, if he called the keys blues and E flat, well, that meant that he, that was his, and he was going to take most of it. And then we played the tunes of the day, like Tartle in Chicago, you know. We played those things. And then we had several rags, like Temptation rags, and just a little bit of Scott Joplin in it. It was still, some people still liked to dance to it, because it had that, well, it was rhythmic.
I suppose that was often a piano feature.
